content: Time is the quietest physician; allow the seasons to do their work.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Toki ga kusuri (時が薬) — Classical Kotowaza
explanation: When an emotional wound is fresh, we frantically seek immediate cures, distractions, or quick fixes. But just as winter cannot be accelerated into spring by human decree, deep healing obeys its own quiet seasons. Trust the faithful medicine of time.
practicalInsight: If you are in pain today, surrender the urge to feel instantly healed. Just survive today and let time do its invisible mending.
reflectionPrompt: Where are you demanding immediate recovery from a wound that simply needs the patient passage of seasons?
